title: Finland and Sweden apply to join NATO
body:
On 18 May 2022 Finland and Sweden formally applied to join NATO. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg received the letters from the two countries' ambassadors at NATO headquarters in Brussels. He said, "I warmly welcome the requests by Finland and Sweden to join NATO. You are our closest partners," and called it "a historic moment, which we must seize."

All 30 NATO members had to weigh the applications, a step expected to take about two weeks. If objections were resolved and accession talks went well, the two countries could join within a few months, compared with the usual 8 to 12 months. Canada said it expected to ratify the accession protocol within days. Some allies, notably the United Kingdom, offered security assurances to the two countries during the application period.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan expressed reservations and took a hard line, saying the Swedish and Finnish delegations should not bother travelling to Ankara. Turkey accuses Sweden, and to a lesser extent Finland, of backing groups it considers terrorist. Sweden had maintained arms sanctions on Turkey since Turkey's 2019 cross-border operation into Syria.
